factual_claims.source_evidence: The Group's working capital position was negative by € 2.7 million as at the year end 31 December 2025 (negative by € 0.7 million as at 31 December 2024)... management plans to liquidate negative working capital by selling properties... preliminary salepurchase agreement... will be concluded... no later than 30.06.2026.

factual_claims.claim: The Admirali Quarter was transferred to the parent through a 2025 merger, while permits and design work for the development were completed.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: On 30.07.2025, Nordic Fibreboard AS and Pärnu Riverside Development OÜ entered into a merger agreement... As a result of the merger, the owner and manager of the Suur-Jõe 48 property is Nordic Fibreboard AS... Building permits have been issued... design work... has been completed.

numerical_claims.claim: Nordic Fibreboard AS reported a difficult 2025, with revenue declining 3.4% to €7.328 million from €7.592 million in 2024.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated net sales for 2025 were € 7.33 million, which is a decrease of 3.4% compared to 2024 sales of € 7.59 million.

numerical_claims.claim: Fibreboard production and sales generated €7.325 million, down from €7.567 million, while real-estate management revenue fell to €3 thousand from €25 thousand following the termination of rental agreements in August 2024.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Sales revenue from the production of fibreboard was € 7.33 million in 2025 (2024: € 7.57 million). Sales revenue in 2025 from real estate management was € 3 thousand (2024: € 25 thousand).

numerical_claims.claim: EBITDA fell to a loss of €420 thousand from a loss of €25 thousand, reducing the EBITDA margin from 0% to negative 6%.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT

numerical_claims.claim: The fibreboard segment moved from EBITDA of €26 thousand to negative €296 thousand, while the real-estate segment’s EBITDA loss widened from €48 thousand to €86 thousand.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Fibreboards production and sales | (296) | 26; Real Estate Management | (86) | (48)

numerical_claims.claim: Gross profit declined to €603 thousand from €771 thousand, despite cost of goods sold decreasing modestly to €6.725 million from €6.820 million.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Gross profit(loss) | 603 | 771; Cost of goods sold | (6,725) | (6,820)

numerical_claims.claim: Distribution costs increased to €982 thousand from €935 thousand and administrative expenses to €502 thousand from €381 thousand.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT

numerical_claims.claim: Other operating expenses also rose to €78 thousand from €11 thousand, including €40 thousand of penalties and €18 thousand from fixed-asset write-offs.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Other operating expenses | 78 | 11; Penalties paid | 40 | 3; Loss of write-off of fixed assets | 18 | 0

numerical_claims.claim: Consequently, the operating loss increased to €940 thousand from €547 thousand, and the net loss widened to €1.154 million from €786 thousand.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Operating profit(loss) | (940) | (547); Net profit(loss) for the period | (1,154) | (786)

numerical_claims.claim: Loss per share improved to €0.14 from €0.17 because the share count increased from 4.499 million to 8.499 million.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Basic loss per share | (0.14) | (0.17); Weighted average number of shares | 8,499 | 4,499

numerical_claims.claim: Personnel, maintenance and repair costs continued during the shutdown and had an approximately €0.2 million negative impact on fibreboard EBITDA.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: the own production of goods more expensive... had a roughly € 0.2 million negative impact on EBITDA.

numerical_claims.claim: The company also reported weak domestic demand and limited willingness by households and businesses to invest amid modest Estonian economic growth, inflation of around 6%, and challenging construction-market conditions.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: inflation... reached around 6% for the year as a whole

numerical_claims.claim: Operating cash flow deteriorated to a €503 thousand outflow from a €174 thousand outflow in 2024.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Net cash generated from operating activities | (503) | (174)

numerical_claims.claim: Investing cash outflow increased to €989 thousand, including €1.367 million invested in production assets and €161 thousand in real estate.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Net cash used in investing activities | (989) | (289); Purchase of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets | (1,367) | (178); Purchase of real estate investment | (161) | (111)

numerical_claims.claim: Financing generated €1.444 million, supported by a €2 million share issue completed in October and related-party financing.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Net cash(used in)/from financing activities | 1,444 | 509; Share capital increase | 2,000 | 0

numerical_claims.claim: Cash nevertheless declined to €5 thousand from €53 thousand.
numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
